title: Gravitational Anomaly in Wide Binary Stars Persists Despite Strict Data Control
oneliner: New research shows that even with the strictest data selection and accounting for hidden stellar companions, the anomalous boost in gravity at low accelerations remains robust.
description: An international team of astronomers has revisited the recent debates about gravity's behavior in wide binary star systems. Analyzing Gaia satellite data using three different samples, the scientists concluded: none of the proposed data 'cleaning' methods or ways of accounting for hierarchical syste
abstract: Objective: Re-examine gravitational tests in wide binaries using 2D velocities. Method: Analysis of the acceleration plane, the distribution of normalized relative velocity (ratio of measured speed to Newtonian circular speed), and its median profile. Result: Rigorous data control and realistic modeling of multiple systems do not eliminate the low-acceleration gravitational anomaly but confirm it—the boost factor γ ≈ 1.3–1.6 agrees with MOND predictions and numerical orbit calculations. Studies that denied the anomaly were erroneous due to calibration of the multiple-system fraction assuming Newtonian dynamics, biased quality cuts, or insufficient statistics. These findings strengthen modified gravity as an alternative to dark matter.
threads: Два фигуриста на бескрайнем льду. Их танец едва заметен — но что-то подо льдом разгоняет их быстрее, чем положено. Именно так ведёт себя гравитация в широких двойных звёздах: данные Gaia трижды подтвердили упрямую аномалию. Если эффект реален, тёмная материя может оказаться миражом, а учебники физики затрещат по швам.

title: Robot Tour Guides: Why a Pair Is Better Than One
oneliner: A duo of a robot and a hologram partner makes a museum tour not just a spectacle but a way to absorb facts more deeply, especially for women.
description: Researchers turned the tour into a show: a real robot guide got a holographic assistant. Comparing a solo format, a projection, and a mixed pair on 30 visitors showed that interest was high in all, but recall improved for women with the duo. Participants unanimously preferred the lively conversation
abstract: A museum guide system is proposed, combining a physical robot and a projected virtual agent that jointly lead tours in a conversational mode. A within-subjects study (30 participants) was conducted to evaluate engagement, experience quality, and learning effectiveness while varying conversational style and agent configuration; data collection included surveys, behavioral sensors, and interviews. Engagement and experience quality were shown to be independent of conditions, whereas learning effectiveness exhibited a significant gender-moderated effect: in hybrid conditions (robot plus virtual agent), women's outcomes improved. Subjectively, all participants preferred the two-agent team, emphasizing the importance of interactivity. The findings highlight that conversational interaction style can differentially influence learning based on gender.

title: Smart Filter for Secret Keys: Autoencoder vs. Noise
oneliner: An autoencoder removes noise from a radio signal, helping two devices obtain a shared reliable secret key.
description: A new method uses an autoencoder—a program that learns to clear noise from a signal, like wiping a fogged-up window. That way, two phones see an identical random picture of the radio channel and can craft a shared secret key, even in heavy interference. The keys turn out stronger, with almost zero e
abstract: To generate secret keys from a wireless channel, we propose using a denoising autoencoder (DAE) that suppresses noise-induced reciprocity imperfections from channel measurements, dramatically improving reliability and efficiency. The autoencoder captures the internal structure of input distributions, restores the original data structure, and removes additive noise while preserving the essential signal structure. The proposed SKG scheme is shown to outperform traditional ones in key disagreement rate (KDR), secret key capacity (SKC), and randomness of generated keys. These results confirm enhanced performance and reliability of physical-layer security systems.

title: How to Pack a Million Shades into a Tiny Box
oneliner: The method packs millions of shades, grouping them like candies in a box, so video chips instantly deliver a smooth picture.
description: Virtual worlds are made of colored dots whose shade depends on the viewing angle. Storing this data is a gluttonous task. Engineers proposed compressing them by grouping similar shades, like candies in a box. The graphics card instantly extracts the average color with a tiny correction, without sacr
abstract: 3D reconstruction methods from image sets, such as 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), use spherical harmonics (SH) to model view-dependent color, leading to a large number of coefficients and high memory demands. The paper proposes compressing SH coefficients using GPU hardware-accelerated texture compression formats (BC1, BC7). It shows that grouping primitives by color and reordering them outperforms compressing regular 2D textures in efficiency. A bitrate control strategy is introduced, preserving random access and scalable rendering parallelization without sacrificing performance. Experiments demonstrate that GPU decompression provides visual quality virtually indistinguishable from the original, with significant memory reduction.

title: How to Weigh the Invisible: Redshift Tomography of Unresolved Galaxies from Euclid and LSST Data
oneliner: Scientists have reconstructed for the first time the redshift distribution of a galaxy population that cannot be seen individually, using multi-band background maps and neural network flows.
description: A new study proposes a method to estimate the redshift distribution of unresolved galaxies directly from multi-band maps of the cosmic optical background. Using conditional normalizing flows trained on realistic image simulations from Euclid and LSST, the model achieves subpercent accuracy in determ
abstract: For unresolved galaxy populations, a methodology is proposed for estimating redshift distributions from multi-band background maps using conditional normalizing flows trained on realistic simulations. With image quality expected from the synergy of Euclid and Rubin LSST, sub-percent accuracy (mean and standard deviation of flux-weighted distributions) is achieved with statistical sample correspondence. The method is robust to photometric incompleteness through imputation. Reliability diagnostics are built in by including observational quantities as target variables. Tomography at the map level is demonstrated: pixel-level details are preserved, yielding nearly sub-percent accuracy for tomographic subsamples. This opens the way to component separation, signal interpretation, and cosmological inferences from optical background fluctuations.
threads: Тусклое свечение космического фона — не брак оптики, а хор из 90% галактик, не видимых поодиночке. Подобно чтению палимпсеста, мы научились разделять этот свет на слои времени и определять расстояние до каждого 'голоса' с точностью менее 1%. Однажды это позволит разглядеть самые первые звёзды Вселенной.

title: Strongly Mixed Worlds: How Inflation Becomes a Cosmic Collider
oneliner: Exact analytical solutions reveal extraordinarily strong signals from heavy particles in the non-Gaussianity of the cosmic microwave background, turning the early Universe into an accelerator of ultimate energies.
description: In a new study, a non-perturbative mathematical framework has been developed to calculate non-Gaussianity in two-field inflationary models with strong mixing between curvature and isocurvature modes. Using exact mode functions, the authors summed mixing effects to all orders and obtained closed-form
abstract: An analytical approach to primordial non-Gaussianity in multi-field inflation has been developed, non-perturbative in the parameter λ describing the mixing of curvature and isocurvature modes. From exact linear solutions for perturbations ζ and σ, propagators are constructed, and exact integral representations are obtained for tree-level bispectra generated by interactions of the form ζ̇²σ, ζ̇σ², and σ³. The approach sums all orders of transfer between perturbations and is applicable for any values of the entropic mass μ. In the strong mixing regime, where standard perturbation theory breaks down, the power spectrum and bispectrum are significantly enhanced, revealing new non-perturbative scaling laws for the amplitude of non-Gaussianity. These results open up possibilities for analytical description of multi-field inflation beyond weak coupling, as well as for analyzing signals of the cosmological collider, formation of primordial black holes, and loop corrections.
threads: В первые мгновения после Большого взрыва Вселенная была коллайдером с энергией, недоступной земным технологиям. Её эхо хранит следы тяжёлых частиц. Как мощный блендер, сильное смешивание полей взбило эти сигналы до гигантских амплитуд. Новый математический аппарат позволяет их уловить — и, возможно, выйти на след тёмной материи.

title: Self-Taught Algorithm: How to Hear a Melody from Noise
oneliner: A new adaptive data recovery method tunes its own parameters, achieving near-perfect accuracy even with rough initial errors.
description: A new adaptive method automatically picks parameters to reconstruct a signal from scattered data. It works like a musician tuning an instrument by ear to blend with the orchestra, despite the noise. The algorithm adjusts its internal model on the fly. This is especially valuable when restoring image
abstract: Approximate message passing (AMP) methods speed up Bayesian inference in high-dimensional inverse problems, but their state evolution predictions depend on exact module parameter specification. An adaptive score-based vector AMP (SC-VAMP) version has been developed. Each factor is updated by a local biased EM step that reuses already computed biased moments of the one-input-one-output interface. Under large-system state evolution and identifiability assumptions, the matched parameters form a Bayes-optimal fixed point. The derivation separates prior modules from likelihood/LMMSE modules; for the latter, a Gaussian cavity arising from the VAMP transformed error model is employed. In numerical experiments on linear and one-bit compressed sensing with a Bernoulli-Gaussian model, the method recovers near-oracle performance even when starting from extremely inaccurate initializations.

title: How to read an enemy in the sky in seconds
oneliner: Combat algorithms learn to make decisions from scraps of data, honestly acknowledging uncertainty.
description: A new air combat algorithm acts like an experienced goalkeeper: from the first patchy radar signals, it predicts the target type and maneuvers, not afraid to admit doubts. In tests — 88% accuracy for class, 93% for intentions.
abstract: Rapid classification of aerial targets and prediction of their intentions are critical for tactical decisions in combat aviation. Standard time-series models require lengthy observations, which is unacceptable with rapidly changing threats. An integrated approach is proposed that enables decision-making from partial data: predictions are generated from short consecutive subsamples, then results are refined by propagating beliefs between them. Classifier outputs are combined using evidential (Dempster-Shafer) reasoning, which reduces uncertainty. Target intentions are inferred through rules and a distance-based method of information fusion over time. Due to the lack of public data, a custom dataset was created, on which the method achieved 88% accuracy for target type classification and 93% for intention prediction in a case with eight aircraft.

title: Random Walks of Dust Grains Around Black Holes and Low-Frequency X-ray Variability
oneliner: Spacetime curvature changes the probabilities of particle capture by a black hole and shapes the observed power spectrum of accreting systems.
description: In a fresh bit of research, scientists looked at how a black hole’s geometry messes with the random dance of dust specks in a churning accretion disk. Cracking the Fokker–Planck equation in the curved spacetime of a Schwarzschild–de Sitter setup, they discovered something counterintuitive: the chanc
abstract: The stochastic dynamics of a dust grain in a turbulent flow with strong gravity is described as a random walk on a Riemannian manifold, modeling the variability of accretion onto compact objects. Solving the Fokker-Planck equation in a black hole background shows that due to the stretching of radial cells near the event horizon, a particle has a higher escape probability than in flat space, since the available volume increases. Modeling the trajectories of many grains distributed on concentric shells according to the structure of a thin accretion disk revealed flux spectra through the horizon: low-frequency slopes become shallower (due to relativistic time dilation), while high-frequency slopes become steeper. The resulting spectra in the Schwarzschild metric reproduce well the observations of low-frequency X-ray variability of Cygnus X-1 in the hard state, highlighting the importance of geometric wandering in accretion.
threads: Чёрная дыра — не пылесос, а батут: кривизна статистически отбрасывает пылинки к космологическому горизонту. Это открытие меняет взгляд на аккрецию и обещает новый инструмент для проверки общей теории относительности — по временным рядам рентгеновской переменности.

title: Why Genes Disrupt the Family Tree
oneliner: Why gene stories don't match the evolution of species, and how a mathematical model helps unravel the tangle.
description: In evolution, genes don't always follow in the species' footsteps. Random loss of variants or direct exchange between unrelated species muddles the picture. Researchers built a simple model of these transfers to understand how often they create the illusion of a different kinship.
abstract: The work revisits a simple model of lateral gene transfer (LGT), where transfer events follow a Poisson process with a constant rate. The analysis focuses on cases of two and three species, for which analytical probabilities of gene trees and site patterns are derived. Implications for identifiability of model parameters are discussed. Moreover, the ability to distinguish between LGT and incomplete lineage sorting (ILS) within given probabilistic models is explored. Practical applications are addressed, and future prospects are outlined.

title: Early Infrared Excess and the Birth of a Corona in Tidal Disruption Event 2024aepd
oneliner: Observations of a disrupted star unveil the secrets of accretion coronae and the mysterious infrared glow.
description: In the tidal disruption event 2024aepd, when a star was torn apart by a supermassive black hole, near-infrared observations revealed an unexpected excess of radiation as early as 40 days. Its spectrum—a nearly flat power-law continuum—does not match the Rayleigh-Jeans tail of ultraviolet blackbody r
abstract: We present multi-wavelength observations of the tidal disruption event TDE 2024aepd, covering primarily the first ~300 days after detection. The X-ray spectrum was initially dominated by a thermal disk component with a hard excess; starting around day 178, the spectrum became a power law and subsequently hardened, indicating rapid formation of a hot corona. An early near-infrared excess was recorded by day ~40; its nearly flat spectrum strongly differs from the Rayleigh-Jeans tail of the ultraviolet-optical blackbody emission. Although a traditional dust echo explanation cannot be entirely ruled out, free-free emission from a reprocessing photospheric shell appears more plausible. The shift in the break between UV-optical and near-IR bands, with a nearly constant density profile index, suggests evolving reprocessing conditions within a weakly changing density structure. TDE 2024aepd becomes the third event (after AT2019azh and TDE 2025abcr) to show an early IR excess; assessing the prevalence of this phenomenon requires a larger sample with near-IR observations at early epochs.
threads: В считанные недели после того, как чёрная дыра разрывает звезду, рождается горячая корона — область, где фотоны взмывают до рентгеновских энергий, словно оркестр берёт крещендо. Инфракрасный избыток, подобный низкому басу, разносит эхо переработанного излучения. Понимание этих процессов — ключ к разгадке роста сверхмассивных чёрных дыр и рождения галактик.

title: Visualization of Spontaneous Vortices in a Disordered Superconducting Nanocomposite
oneliner: Using scanning SQUID microscopy, scientists captured unusually extended and entangled spontaneous vortices emerging during a phase transition in an MgO/MgB₂ nanocomposite, demonstrating their connection to the Kibble–Zurek mechanism.
description: For the first time, detailed images have been obtained of spontaneous quantized vortices in a superconducting nanocomposite with induced (proximity-effect) superconductivity, composed of randomly distributed MgB₂ grains in an MgO matrix. Unlike conventional Abrikosov vortices induced by an external
abstract: Spontaneous symmetry breaking during a continuous second-order phase transition in superconductors was investigated, leading to the formation of topological defects — quantized vortices. Using a scanning SQUID microscope, spontaneous vortices were visualized in a superconducting nanocomposite with the proximity effect. Under near-zero field conditions, vortices with different polarities, sizes, and shapes are stochastically observed. Their field distributions are more extended and complex than those of field-induced Abrikosov vortices, and the effective penetration depth ranges from ~1 to ~10 μm. Spontaneous vortices arise upon cooling as a result of competition between Josephson coupling and thermal phase fluctuations inherent to proximity-effect systems. The vortex morphology apparently captures information about local phase differences that existed at an early stage of the transition, offering a glimpse into the process of order emergence.
threads: Космические струны — гипотетические складки пространства-времени — возможно, застыли в первые мгновения после Большого взрыва. Сегодня физики нашли их миниатюрное подобие в куске сверхпроводящей керамики. Запутанные магнитные вихри, самопроизвольно возникшие при охлаждении, — это отпечаток фазового перехода, словно фотография рождения порядка. Изучая их, мы, возможно, поймём, как Вселенная обретала структуру.

title: Magnetic Bridge Through Earth: Relay Boosts Communication
oneliner: Engineers found a way to speed up magnetic communication through the ground using a repeater.
description: Magnetic fields penetrate the ground where radio waves fail. A new method adds a repeater — a device that amplifies the signal — and allows precise calculation of how much faster data transfer becomes. The solutions will be useful in mines, subways, and underwater exploration.
abstract: Magnetic induction (MI) communication is used in through-the-earth scenarios: mines, underground rivers. To boost data rate, a cooperative MI (CMI) scheme with an amplify-and-forward (AF) relay is proposed. Unlike prior work, the focus is on arbitrary relay antenna position and orientation (antenna deployment). A closed-form expression is derived for the achievable CMI rate gain (CMG) and a closed-form expression for the CMI channel bandwidth. Simulation results show that a relay with appropriate antenna deployment can yield significant increase in achievable rate in MI systems.

title: How a Self-Driving Car Builds a Map from Above
oneliner: Scientists trained a computer to piece together a road map from fragmented snapshots, sifting through possible variations.
description: The computer generates several draft maps and picks the best one, merging camera data as if looking out of different windows. This approach makes lane marking recognition reliable even in bad weather.
abstract: The task of bird’s-eye view (BEV) segmentation from multiple cameras is framed within variational inference. A transformer network, TVB, is proposed, which implicitly learns to map multiple viewpoints into a canonical BEV map based on posterior control. It builds on a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) that generates several map candidates. To enhance realism, normalizing flows are incorporated into the generation process, enabling complex distributions. A BEV attention module (BAF) is developed, which uses attention mechanisms to adaptively combine several candidates into the final map. Experiments on the nuScenes and OPV2V datasets demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method in BEV segmentation and road perception tasks.

title: The Complexity of Crowds: Why Averages Fail
oneliner: CWMMSE measures complexity, seeing not the average picture, but the full diversity of hidden patterns.
description: CWMMSE measures the complexity of trajectory sets by grouping similar paths and assessing not only their entanglement but also the differences between groups. It turns out: a calm ocean is more complex than a stormy one due to hidden diversity of currents, and heart disease reduces not overall chaos
abstract: For analyzing trajectory ensembles (from chaotic flows to clinical cohorts), a cluster-weighted multidimensional multiscale sample entropy (CWMMSE) is proposed. The method splits trajectories into behavioral patterns and weights each group by its dynamical complexity, separating individual complexity from population diversity. The empirical plug-in estimator is strictly consistent for a fixed finite partition. CWMMSE reveals that these two components can diverge in real data: averaging ignores diversity, while a dispersion-only metric might mistake a diverse but predictable population for a complex one. Across eleven physical, engineering, and biomedical systems, the method assigns a higher rank to a calm oceanic region than to an energetic but homogeneous one; identifies a strong earthquake as a collapse of systemic complexity; and overturns conclusions in cardiac cohorts where diseases reduce population diversity. Results are backed by an open reproducible implementation and show that population complexity should be measured, not averaged.

title: WanSong: Songs from Noise in One Step
oneliner: The WanSong neural network turns random noise into songs up to five minutes long with vocals and instruments.
description: WanSong works like a sculptor: it transforms noise into music by removing the excess step by step. Unlike other models, it creates multi-track songs straight away, with no intermediate stages, and automatically separates vocals and instruments. This makes editing easier.
abstract: WanSong is a diffusion model for song generation, capable of directly producing high-quality audio up to 5 minutes long in several languages. Unlike autoregressive and cascade designs, it outputs two separate tracks (vocals and background music) in a single forward pass. Step distillation speeds up inference, while an efficient fine-tuning mechanism allows adaptation for editing tasks. The approach achieves commercial-grade quality and is suitable for industrial use.

title: Boson Peak Reveals Nano-Secrets of Cement Gel
oneliner: Terahertz spectroscopy and low-temperature calorimetry have for the first time detected the boson peak in concrete's main component, linking it to elastic heterogeneity at the nanoscale.
description: Scientists have experimentally discovered the boson peak — a universal anomaly in the vibrational spectrum of disordered media — in calcium silicate hydrate (C-S-H), the primary binding phase of hardened cement. Using terahertz spectroscopy and low-temperature heat capacity measurements, they showed
abstract: The boson peak (BP), a universal vibrational anomaly of disordered media, has been systematically characterized in calcium silicate hydrate (C-S-H), the binding phase of hardened cement, for five Ca/Si ratios (0.5–1.7). Using time-domain terahertz spectroscopy and low-temperature calorimetry after Bruggeman correction for impurities, the BP is localized near 1 THz. The integrated spectral weight and the peak in Cp/T³ decrease monotonically with increasing Ca/Si, while the terahertz peak amplitude is maximum at Ca/Si = 1.0, reflecting a structural crossover between depolymerization of silicate chains and filling of interlayer space by calcium. From BP analysis, a dynamic correlation length of ~1 nm (0.3–2 nm) and an elastic heterogeneity parameter γ are obtained, decreasing from 0.98 to 0.48. The BP frequency, normalized to the Debye frequency (ν_BP/ν_D = 0.15–0.17), falls within the range of silicate glasses. The parameter γ, governing the distribution of energy barriers for local rearrangements, becomes a quantitative composition-dependent descriptor of intrinsic creep and heat transport in C-S-H, linking nanoscale dynamics to macroscopic concrete durability.
threads: Представьте барабан, натянутый неравномерно: его звук выдаёт распределение напряжений. Бозонный пик в цементе — такой же «голос» наномира: частота ~1 ТГц раскрывает флуктуации жёсткости на наномасштабе. Управляя этим гулом, мы создадим бетон, который не ползёт веками — и однажды, возможно, отправится на Марс.

title: Ghost Echoes Make Radar More Precise
oneliner: A receiver defect that creates false reflections paradoxically improves radar clarity.
description: Radar signals are split into multiple frequencies. The slightest electronic imbalance spawns phantom copies of targets. Instead of suppressing them, they're used alongside the real ones—accuracy soars.
abstract: In OFDM-based ISAC systems, receiver quadrature imbalance (IQI) couples each subcarrier with its mirror, generating false targets and degrading range-Doppler recovery. Instead of compensating for IQI, we propose leveraging the structure of the distorted observation: it is shown that each physical target produces linked direct and mirror components, expressed through the target coefficient and its conjugate, which motivates a representation as an elliptical group of atoms for each hypothetical delay-Doppler cell. Based on this model, an elliptical group detector of the orthogonal matching pursuit type is developed, performing sparse recovery directly on the received OFDM grid. The required correlations are efficiently computed via two weighted two-dimensional FFTs and local group projections. Numerical results show improved carrier recovery accuracy and weak target detection compared to existing methods, especially under moderate to strong IQI.

title: Radar Sculptor: How Radio Waves Sculpt a Drone's Portrait
oneliner: The technology turns reflected signals into a three-dimensional sculpture, revealing a drone's shape and movement.
description: Scientists trained radar to reconstruct a drone's appearance and notice the slightest changes — down to a light payload. The method outperforms optics in fog and darkness.
abstract: The task of radar sensing and tracking of UAVs: a base station with an antenna array illuminates the craft and from reflections builds a point cloud containing spatial and electromagnetic characteristics. This allows to uniformly extract position, orientation, and shape. To solve the complex inverse problem, the AUGUST method is proposed, including conditional channel encoding with position and SNR embeddings for robustness to rapid changes, and generative decoding based on a diffusion model with weighted training. The encoder projects features into a latent space regularized by a flow-based prior distribution. Simulation demonstrates AUGUST's superiority in point cloud reconstruction accuracy, yielding better recovery of orientation and shape, as well as a significant gain in positioning accuracy compared to the classical model-based approach.

title: Radar Without Ghosts: A New 'Melody' Against False Targets
oneliner: Engineers composed a radio pulse 'melody' that rids radar of ghost targets while keeping the picture sharp.
description: To cut costs, radar signal processing is 'compressed', but ghost targets appear—like off-key notes in a poor recording. Previous pulse designs gave either clarity with many ghosts or purity at the cost of smearing. The new SC-EFM modulation is a distinct waveform that almost eliminates 'false notes'
abstract: Sub-Nyquist sampling in wideband pulse compression radars produces coherent false targets due to spectral aliasing. LFM pulses yield a compact response but are ghost-sensitive; HFM pulses suppress ghosts but degrade range resolution. A SC-EFM (sine-over-cosine Jacobi elliptic frequency-modulated waveform) is proposed, where the elliptic modulus controls the instantaneous frequency curvature while maintaining duration and bandwidth. The sub-Nyquist convolution structure is analytically described, and closed-form expressions for detection probabilities are derived. Simulations showed that SC-EFM significantly reduces false alarm rates compared to LFM, while preserving resolution, and outperforms HFM in distinguishing nearby targets. This is a unified solution for ghost-robust multi-channel ranging.

title: How the Brain Conducts Attention: A Meditation Model
oneliner: A new model explains how the brain manages attention: like an experienced conductor, it learns to quickly notice distractions and gently return to the main focus.
description: Scientists simulated meditation on a computer, identifying four states: focus on breathing, mind wandering, awareness of distraction, and return. Comparing beginners and experts revealed that experienced meditators recognize distractions faster and shift more smoothly. The model links subjective exp
abstract: Meditative mastery involves sustained attention, rapid disengagement from distractions, and coordination of brain networks. A computational phenomenology of focused attention meditation is presented, with four states: focus on breath, mind-wandering, meta-awareness, and attention return. The dual active inference model features a three-level architecture: (L1) Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process on Yeo networks; (L2) System 1—a generative model with thoughtseeds, evaluating action tendencies; (L3) System 2—a metacognitive monitor using the global workspace bottleneck to gate these tendencies. Meta-awareness as a global ignition signal arises from policy-expectation mismatch and is regulated by competition between orchestrating and distracting thoughtseeds. Policies are selected by minimizing expected free energy, and L2 actions generate top-down predictions, closing the perception-action loop. Variational EM training on expert and novice phenotypes reproduces empirical patterns, linking phenomenology to neurophysiology.

title: Compressing networks: when roads become points
oneliner: Scientists found a clever way to compress numeric networks: lines become dots, and barely noticeable fluctuations are discarded.
description: A new method for packing numeric maps (like road networks with traffic). First, the map is transformed: roads become nodes, and intersections become edges between them. Then numeric values are decomposed into simple waves, and weak ones are discarded. The rest are encoded very densely. A smoothness
abstract: A compression scheme for weighted graphs is proposed: topology is transmitted losslessly, edge weights are lossy. To disambiguate edge relationships, the graph is transformed into its line graph, where nodes correspond to original edges, and edges represent adjacency. Edge weights are interpreted as a graph signal on the line graph and transformed by a bank of graph filters. Coefficients are then quantized and entropy coded. An edge smoothness measure is introduced, formalizing compression complexity and computable without building the line graph. Experiments on synthetic and real data show superiority over existing matrix preprocessing methods.

title: Flying Radio Mirror: A Drone That Steers Its Own Signal
oneliner: A flying radio mirror adjusts in real time to the drone's shaking, keeping the signal pristine.
description: A prototype smart surface on a drone acts as a self-aiming mirror for radio signals. Even in flight, when the drone shakes, the mirror predicts displacements and instantly reorients itself—keeping the link perfect.
abstract: The first fully functional, real-time prototype of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) mounted on an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is presented. Experimental measurements under realistic disturbance conditions confirm that the RIS position can be predicted using an extended Kalman filter and the UAV’s onboard sensors. Employing this estimate for dynamic RIS reconfiguration in real time effectively compensates for motion and vibration effects, preserving the channel capacity improvement. A systematic evaluation of various placement options revealed practical characteristics of RIS operation in field scenarios. This experimental validation bridges the gap between theoretical studies and actual hardware constraints, demonstrating the feasibility of UAV–RIS systems for adaptive propagation environment control in future sixth-generation wireless networks.

title: How Robots Negotiate the Noisy Airwaves
oneliner: Reliable radio communication between robots improves movement accuracy and saves energy.
description: Random delays in the wireless network confuse robots. Engineers tested different transmission modes in a 5G network: reliable signal delivery improved accuracy by 51.5% compared to the usual approach.
abstract: For navigation with dynamic collision avoidance under stochastic delays and variable wireless reliability, an extended quality of control (QoC) model is proposed, adapted to practical robotic systems. The method includes end-to-end modeling of network impact on the closed-loop control and systematic analysis of how robot motion parameters affect delay and channel reliability. Experimental validation was performed on a private 5G testbed with varying delays, reliability, and controller settings. Optimal co-design modes of the control system and communications for real robots were identified. Comparison of standard Quality of Service (QoS) policies in ROS 2 showed that RELIABLE mode provides a 51.5% higher QoC score than BEST-EFFORT under certain experimental conditions.

title: How Curvature Turns Phonon Hall Viscosity into Angular Momentum
oneliner: Theoretically demonstrated: in curved crystal membranes, flexural vibrations generate directional phonon angular momentum thanks to Hall viscosity.
description: In a flat membrane, the fundamental flexural mode does not interact with phonon Hall viscosity. However, static curvature converts normal motion into in-plane shear strain, opening a channel sensitive to the Hall response. We show that this coupling generates in-plane phonon angular momentum, direct
abstract: In a flat crystalline membrane, the low-energy spectrum is dominated by bending modes that don't couple to the phonon Hall viscosity. Static curvature converts normal displacements into in-plane strain, opening a Hall channel. The traceless curvature directly couples to the Hall shear, while the mean curvature couples indirectly through ordinary elastic shear. Together they generate an in-plane phonon angular momentum. For a statistically isotropic gentle ripple, the time average yields a stationary odd-in-field torque proportional to the mean-square curvature, with sign governed by the Hall viscosity. An estimate based on the bulk Hall viscosity of α-RuCl₃ predicts a torque of ~10⁻²² N·m for a membrane a few atomic layers thick—within reach of existing torsion sensors. This bending-to-shear response is a direct route to measuring phonon Hall viscosity in atomically thin crystals.
threads: В крошечной изогнутой мембране из магнитного кристалла звуковые волны не просто колеблются — они начинают вращаться. Кривизна играет роль дирижёра: без неё холловская вязкость — таинственная «смазка», не создающая трения, — остаётся безмолвной. Так рождается постоянный угловой момент, измеримый теми же датчиками, что ловят гравитационные волны. Мы на пороге тепловых гироскопов без движущихся деталей — только геометрия и квантовая фаза.

title: AI Plans Radiation Therapy in Two Minutes
oneliner: Artificial intelligence independently and accurately builds a radiation plan for a cancerous tumor from daily scans—in just two minutes.
description: Scientists have created an AI agent that fully automates the daily preparation for radiation therapy. It processes a CT scan, identifies tumor boundaries, calculates doses, and suggests settings—all in two minutes. A doctor supervises the key steps. As a result, treatment speeds up, the burden on me
abstract: A unified agent system based on a foundation model for fully automated 'one-for-all' adaptive radiation therapy planning is presented. Using daily cone-beam CT data, the agent predicts a synthetic CT, performs multimodal registration and segmentation of the tumor and organs at risk within two minutes, and then generates a complete treatment plan. The system supports 'human-in-the-loop': the clinician sets objectives and intervenes at critical points. On patient cohorts with head and neck, lung, abdominal, and prostate tumors, for both photon and proton therapy, target dose errors (D98) did not exceed 2.0 Gy compared to reference plans. The results confirm the promise of universal foundation models for fast and scalable adaptive radiation therapy.

title: Why photo enhancement software fails on unfamiliar images
oneliner: Photo cleanup programs stumble on unfamiliar images because they take steps in the wrong direction. But a quick tweak with a few examples corrects the course.
description: Photo enhancement software often ruins frames with unusual blur or noise. The culprit isn't a general error, but the algorithm's misdirected steps—it veers off course. By showing it a few examples of proper cleanup, you can adjust its path without a complete overhaul.
abstract: Plug-and-Play proximal gradient descent (PnP-PGD) provides flexibility in image restoration by using denoisers as implicit priors, yet they are often applied outside their training domain. The concept of 'proximal mismatch' is introduced — the discrepancy between the used denoiser and the target proximal mapping of the regularizer. This turns denoising steps into inexact proximal steps. A stationarity bound is derived with a decreasing O(1/K) part and an additive term proportional to the average squared mismatch. The result motivates adaptation via proximal alignment, rather than mere MSE fitting. Two families are studied: learned proximal networks and denoisers based on a gradient step. In experiments on Gaussian deblurring and super-resolution with significant domain shift, proximal alignment substantially improves quality over MSE adaptation, especially in the few-shot regime.

title: A Map That Isn't Afraid to Admit: 'I Don't Know'
oneliner: Robots build a map with guaranteed accuracy, openly admitting where the data is unreliable.
description: Scientists have found a way to fuse data from a group of robots so that the final map directly flags dubious areas. The method works regardless of sensor quality or communication links between the machines.
abstract: Multi-agent mapping demands formal accuracy guarantees. While methods like Gaussian processes offer rich spatial correlation, they lack finite-sample reliability. Conformal prediction locally provides a coverage guarantee, but in practice it degrades due to temporal correlations and limited field of view. Hence, a distributed fusion algorithm is proposed: robots share e-values, which are combined using a neighborhood error budget and an uncertainty-dampening operator. The resulting map is proven to recover the target coverage level irrespective of network topology and sensor noise. The trade-off: with insufficient evidence, the map returns both classes (free and occupied), leaving unclassified zones. Simulations show adherence to theoretical bounds and shrinking unclassified areas with denser topologies.

title: How Spite Replenishes Resources
oneliner: When a resource replenishes slowly, spite unexpectedly allows it to recover, then gives way to fairness.
description: In repeated negotiations over a shared resource, the speed of its replenishment decides everything. Rapid growth encourages fairness, slow growth creates a paradoxical cycle: spite temporarily takes over, but this allows the resource to accumulate and fairness to return.
abstract: A stochastic ultimatum game model is proposed, in which proposer and responder repeatedly interact to allocate a renewable resource belonging to the proposer. Successful agreements deplete the resource, rejections block harvesting and promote recovery. Using mutation-selection stochastic dynamics for two types, the evolution of spitefulness and fairness is studied. A strong dependence on resource growth rate is found: at high rates, fairness prevails; at low rates, a feedback loop emerges, governed by spitefulness. In a depleted state, spiteful behavior dominates, accelerating the transition to a replenished state, where repeated interactions, in turn, promote fairness. The results highlight the critical role of resource recovery pace in shaping social norms.

title: Coloring Black Holes: Choices in Creating the First Image of the Event Horizon
oneliner: One-sentence essence: An analysis of how astrophysicists, using algorithms and data from eight radio telescopes, transformed sparse signals into a single image of a black hole's shadow, and why this image is the result of not only observations but also numerous conscious choices.
description: In 2019, the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) collaboration unveiled the first-ever image of the shadow of a supermassive black hole at the center of galaxy M87. This achievement was a triumph for radio astronomy and computational methods, but its creation required two years of painstaking work and was
abstract: In 2019, the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) collaboration released the first image of a black hole's shadow, obtained from observations. However, the final picture was just one of many plausible visualizations of extremely noisy and sparse data. At every processing step — from calibration to image synthesis — a choice between competing approaches or averaging of their results was required. This paper analyzes the epistemic and aesthetic decisions made by the EHT and shows how a different choice would have changed the final image. The key conclusion: the main scientific value lies not in a single canonical snapshot, but in demonstrating a constrained variability that preserves the key shadow structure intact.
threads: Когда в 2019 году показали снимок чёрной дыры, многие решили, что это фотография. На самом деле, это симфония, собранная по обрывкам партитуры. Восемь антенн по всей планете уловили лишь несколько «нот» от плазмы вокруг M87*. Алгоритмы, словно дирижёры, достроили мелодию — каждый по-своему. Итог — усреднение трёх версий. Следующее поколение добавит космические «уши», и тогда, возможно, мы услышим голос бездны в полную силу.

title: Where Are You? Radio Waves Know the Answer
oneliner: Like a sensitive ear, your phone picks up the unique pattern of radio waves in a room—and from that, figures out exactly where you're standing.
description: Indoors, a radio signal behaves like a note sung in a concert hall: reflections create a one-of-a-kind melody for each spot. A listener program memorizes these invisible chords and uses them to locate you more precisely than GPS. This technology promises navigation in subways and smart factories.
abstract: Localization in wireless systems is examined through a unified model: signal observations — channel representation — location inference. The survey covers learning-based high-accuracy positioning methods, structuring them around channel representations. Typical forms of observations (CSI, delay maps, angular profiles) and their physical meaning are analyzed. Feature extraction and representation learning approaches are reviewed: from handcrafted design to deep networks. Methods are classified by stages of obtaining, organizing, adapting, and reusing representations; compared by accuracy, applicability conditions, data requirements, and generalizability. It is shown that the quality and practical suitability of channel representations decisively affect localization performance. Finally, key challenges in transitioning from lab experiments to real-world deployment are highlighted and directions to overcome them are proposed.

title: How Robots Chart a Course Through a Galaxy of Errors
oneliner: A subtle helm in the digital brain keeps robots from losing their grip, even as the world shifts around them.
description: Robots drop objects when their neural network gets scrambled. Scientists spotted a galaxy in those signals: successful and faulty commands separated like safe and perilous space. So they embedded a helm that steers signals back on course in real time. Now, even with a shaky camera, the grasp holds f
abstract: Mechanistic interpretability uncovered how WAM models encode perturbations critical for robustness. Activation comparisons revealed that in Cosmos-Policy and DiT4DiT architectures, relevant features are linearly separable, unlike in LingBot-VA. This enabled control without fine-tuning by setting contrastive directions in activation space. Local linearity of dynamics allowed synthesizing WA-LQR—a reduced LQR feedback controller. Mechanistic estimates predicted, and experiments confirmed, high controllability for the first two architectures and low for the third. On Cosmos-Policy and DiT4DiT, WA-LQR generalizes contrastive directions to new tasks and improves resilience to camera shifts, noise, and gripper changes.

title: How Noise Creates Diversity
oneliner: Random noise can reinforce, not erase, diversity in a population.
description: A new study flips the script: in the Hawks and Doves game, random fluctuations don’t average out behavior but split the population into warriors and peacemakers, preserving this divide for the long haul.
abstract: In deterministic evolutionary game theory, a monomorphic population with a mixed strategy is indistinguishable from a polymorphic population with pure strategies in corresponding proportions. The "trembling hand" hypothesis suggests that in finite populations, demographic noise promotes monomorphism, but simulations have yielded contradictory results. This discrepancy is resolved by a theoretical analysis of the hawk-dove game using separation of time scales. It is shown that stochastic effects can cause polymorphism, leading to long-lived polymorphic states under certain conditions.

title: Smart Circuits for Clear Signals
oneliner: A new tuning algorithm for radio transmitters turns budget hardware into speed record-holders.
description: When a transmitter has multiple antennas, they need to be matched, otherwise the signal is lost. Scientists developed a method for tuning internal circuits that squeezes maximum speed even from mediocre components.

title: How to Teach AI Not to Confuse Similar MRI Scans
oneliner: Scientists have proposed a method that helps artificial intelligence analyze medical images more accurately, even when they look identical.
description: Typically, during training, AI compares paired data and treats everything else as different. But in medicine, two scans can be very similar even though they belong to different patients. This confuses the AI, leading to errors. The new MseaCL system uses doctors' text reports to understand how simil
abstract: Multimodal contrastive learning usually assumes pairwise matches within a batch, treating all non-matching samples as negatives. In medical data, this leads to false negatives because scans and texts with similar semantics may still be unpaired. The proposed MseaCL method takes into account the semantic closeness of radiology reports to mitigate this effect. The model was trained on a pediatric cohort of 3D brain MRIs and their corresponding reports. Using MseaCL for pretraining raised the AUC of molecular classification of childhood brain tumors by at least 22.6%, highlighting the promise of semantically aware multimodal alignment in clinical tasks.

title: The Galaxy's Chemical Clock: How Yttrium and Magnesium Reveal Stellar Ages
oneliner: A new analysis of 736 stars shows the Y/Mg ratio works as a chemical age indicator, but its calibration depends on position in the disk and metallicity.
description: To overcome the difficulties of directly determining stellar ages, astronomers use 'chemical clocks'—element ratios that change over time. The yttrium-magnesium (Y/Mg) pair draws particular attention: magnesium is rapidly ejected by Type II supernovae, while yttrium accumulates slowly in asymptotic
abstract: Based on a sample of 736 field stars (new atmospheric parameters and Mg and Y abundances, accounting for non-LTE effects, for 528; asteroseismic ages for 307; isochrone ages for 221), spatial variations of the [Y/Mg]–age relation in the Galactic disk are explored. Two new triple and nine double spectroscopic systems are identified. Systematic differences in the [Y/Mg]–age dependence are found, reflecting an inhomogeneous history of star formation and enrichment. Overall, [Y/Mg] rises with metallicity, but at supersolar values the trend weakens and becomes flatter than for solar-metallicity stars, where young ones show lower [Y/Mg] and old ones elevated [Y/Mg].
threads: Звёздный хронометр оказался с географией: во внешнем диске Галактики химические часы на иттрии и магнии спешат, а в толстом — еле ползут. Это открытие рушит миф об универсальном методе датировки и рисует Млечный Путь как оркестр, где каждая секция играет в своём темпе. В будущем многомерные модели машинного обучения восстановят всю историю Галактики по этим разноголосым партитурам.

title: Dark Matter and Neutrinos: Record Limits from Lyman-alpha Lines
oneliner: Analysis of Lyman-alpha forest spectra rules out significant interaction between dark matter and neutrinos, setting the world's strongest limit on the coupling strength.
description: Using full hydrodynamic simulations and a neural network emulator, scientists compared model Lyman-alpha forest spectra with high-resolution data from Keck and VLT telescopes. Bayesian analysis yielded an upper limit on the interaction parameter uνχ ≤ 1.5×10⁻⁸ (95% CI) — a hundred times stricter tha
abstract: New constraints on dark matter models interacting with neutrinos are presented, derived from high-resolution Lyman-alpha forest data. A suite of full hydrodynamic simulations was performed, covering a range of interaction strengths and thermal histories. An emulator was trained on the results, and Bayesian analysis (MCMC) yields an upper limit of uνχ ≤ 1.5×10⁻⁸ (95% confidence level)—the strongest direct constraint to date. The findings rule out previous hints of non-zero interactions. Comparison with approaches that project warm dark matter constraints onto models with suppressed small-scale structures shows that such methods overestimate the predictive power for this model.
threads: Миллиарды лет свет квазаров нёс сквозь космос ноты водородной партитуры. Астрофизики прислушались, надеясь уловить дуэт тёмной материи и нейтрино. Но расслышали лишь абсолютное молчание: взаимодействие оказалось как минимум в сотню раз слабее, чем предполагали смелые гипотезы. Этот предел не просто отсекает модные теории — он заставляет по-новому взглянуть на скрытую жизнь Вселенной.

title: Gene Map Predicts Breast Cancer Outcomes
oneliner: A mathematical cartographer drew a map of the genetic city and found the neighborhood where aggressive breast cancer becomes vulnerable.
description: For a thousand women with breast cancer, scientists created an activity map of genes—each gene like a house, its work the life inside. The mathematical cartographer revealed hidden neighborhoods invisible to standard tests. It turned out that patients from 'quiet' neighborhoods with aggressive cance
abstract: Using the Mapper algorithm from Topological Data Analysis (TDA), gene expression profiles from over 1000 breast cancer patients from the TCGA-BRCA database were analyzed. The constructed network revealed a hidden geometric structure, in which proximity to high-risk regions correlated with significantly worse survival. Highly proliferative expression patterns were associated with unfavorable outcomes, but therapy narrowed this gap. Of particular interest is a subgroup of patients with the basal-like subtype, who showed unexpectedly favorable prognosis due to a unique gene signature more sensitive to treatment. Validation on independent data confirmed that the topologically defined risk groups maintain a significant association with survival after adjusting for age, tumor stage, and treatment. Thus, the geometric structure of gene expression data contains prognostic information not captured by standard breast cancer classification methods.

title: Spinning primordial black holes: a new look at dark matter through cosmic dust heating
oneliner: Taking spin and halo profile into account refines constraints on the fraction of primordial black holes in dark matter that heat interstellar dust.
description: Primordial black holes are intriguing candidates for dark matter. Their Hawking radiation can heat interstellar dust, offering an independent way to estimate their contribution. This new work systematically accounts for black hole spin and various dark matter halo profiles for the first time. It tur
abstract: Primordial black holes (PBHs) with masses in the range 10^15–10^18 g can heat interstellar dust through Hawking radiation. Unlike previous works, the spin of PBHs is considered, which enhances radiation intensity, and the impact of five dark matter distribution models (isothermal, Einasto, NFW, Moore, Burkert) is investigated. Full photon spectra, including primary and secondary emission, are computed. It is shown that for a fixed halo profile and mass function, higher spin values impose stricter constraints on the PBH dark matter fraction f_PBH. The tightest limits come from the isothermal profile, followed by Einasto, NFW, and Moore; the Burkert profile yields the weakest constraints. For silicate dust grains, which cool more slowly than graphite ones, the upper bound on f_PBH reaches 10^{-4} at maximal spin. Both monochromatic and log-normal mass functions are considered; for the log-normal function, increasing the width σ excludes a broader mass range, preventing massive PBHs from being the sole dark matter component. The obtained constraints are weaker than existing ones but serve as an independent check.
threads: Межзвёздная пыль — триллионы микротермометров, разбросанных по Галактике. Они чутко реагируют на малейший нагрев, выдавая местоположение испаряющихся чёрных дыр. Учёт спина показал: даже слабое вращение умножает излучение и затягивает петлю ограничений. Возможно, скоро инфракрасные карты неба станут окном в природу тёмной материи.

title: A Colorful World Through a Single Pixel
oneliner: Adaptive mask switching helps a single pixel distinguish hundreds of shades without expensive optics.
description: Cameras that distinguish hundreds of shades are expensive. A new approach captures such images with a simple sensor: the measurement sequence is tailored to the scene, boosting clarity in visible and near-infrared light.
abstract: An improved approach to single-pixel spectral imaging is proposed, based on end-to-end optimization of the Hadamard basis order with respect to scene characteristics. Unlike static deep optical coding designs (DOCD), the method dynamically generates a sequence of modulation patterns for each frame, maximizing the information content of hundreds of exposures. Validation was performed on spectral datasets and a laboratory prototype: improved quality of reconstructed images in visible and near-infrared ranges was achieved compared to fixed constructions. The solution enables adaptive multispectral capture without feedback on cheap equipment.

title: World in Flickers: How a Camera Assembles an Image from Flashes
oneliner: From a stream of flickers, scientists assembled a detailed picture of the Earth's surface.
description: Regular cameras capture frames. Event-based ones only detect changes in light. Scientists have shown how to assemble a sharp image from these changes, like a puzzle of light shards. Tests on the ISS confirmed: the method distinguishes clouds, islands, and landscape.
abstract: We propose a method to recover the static logarithmic brightness field from a monocular event camera, framing it as an inverse synthetic-aperture problem. Instead of reconstructing a dynamic video volume, we impose a geometric constraint: latent projections are generated from the static scene according to camera motion. Aggregating events over time bins yields a linear model where the temporal difference of these projections (operator A) should equal the signed event counts b plus noise η. The combined operator AP leads to an ill-conditioned system due to averaging and differentiation, so we employ regularized inversion. Experiments on simulated and real Falcon Neuro data with near-vertical motion show that the recovered θ-field recovers large-scale structure, preserving spatial continuity and suppressing textural noise better than methods based on dynamic images.

title: Why Not Every Contact Leads to Illness
oneliner: A new model accounts for infection depending on the amount of virus, which changes over time.
description: Scientists created a model where infection depends on the 'age of infection'—the time since the virus entered the body. This age determines how much virus can be transmitted upon contact. The larger the dose, the higher the chance of getting sick. Such a model predicts epidemic development more accu
abstract: A model of infectious disease spread is presented, incorporating the concept of exposure (contact with the pathogen) in the classical epidemiological sense: the fact of interacting with an infected person does not necessarily lead to infection. The model also uses a discrete age-of-infection structure, which implicitly accounts for the viral load of infected individuals and, consequently, determines the probability of developing infection based on the viral load during contacts. This approach provides a more detailed description of transmission compared to traditional SIR-like models. Studying such models is important for understanding the role of pathogen dose and the temporal dynamics of infectiousness in epidemic development.

title: Lightweight AI for Space Communications: More Accurate and Efficient
oneliner: A tiny AI model predicts radio signal distortions on a satellite, using almost no power.
description: Interference disrupts satellite communications. A new power-efficient AI running directly on board accurately catches signal distortions with minimal energy consumption. This will bring internet to the most remote corners.
abstract: For non-geostationary satellite systems (NTN) in 6G, channel estimation has specific characteristics: high propagation predictability, limited multipath scattering, and significant Doppler shifts. This work proposes a lightweight channel estimator based on convolutional neural networks, designed for on-board real-time execution under strict energy budgets. The model leverages prior knowledge about the channel, yielding an improvement in MSE over classical algorithms (LS, MMSE) and reducing the number of parameters by 27% compared to state-of-the-art AI solutions. Computational complexity is reduced by about 29 times in terms of floating-point operations compared to traditional methods. The results confirm that efficient AI models can reliably operate on power-constrained space nodes, ensuring high link quality with minimal resources.

title: Robot Juggler: Synchronized Play with a Human
oneliner: Engineers have taught a robot to catch and throw balls in rhythm with a human, like an experienced circus duo.
description: The robot has mastered paired juggling with a human: it catches and tosses balls, predicting their flight in a split second. Even beginners achieved record-breaking synchronicity.
abstract: The challenge of dynamic object exchange between humans and robots remains difficult due to perceptual uncertainties, time delays, and contact-rich interactions. Collaborative juggling demands particularly high levels of coordination, predictive motion planning, and robustness to human variability. We propose a real-time architecture for partner juggling that integrates predictive ball tracking, adaptive online trajectory optimization using multiple shooting, and finite-state machine coordination logic. In a study with 8 participants (novices to experts), the system demonstrated a three-ball cascade between robot and human. All participants surpassed previously recorded best performances within a 10-minute session; one participant achieved 20 consecutive robot catches (a fivefold improvement over the previous record), and another showed 100% success over 40 consecutive catches in single-ball catch-and-return mode. These results are significant for advancing physical human-robot interaction and shared autonomy.

title: Most hot Jupiters are born beyond the water ice line
oneliner: Analysis of the atmospheric composition of nine hot Jupiters showed that at least six of them formed beyond the water snow line, pointing to the important role of dynamical interactions in their migration.
description: Scientists used planet formation simulations that included pebble and gas accretion, migration, and chemical processes in the protoplanetary disk to reproduce the carbon and oxygen content in hot Jupiter atmospheres. Comparison with observational data allowed them to constrain their birthplaces rela
abstract: The atmospheric compositions of hot Jupiters were investigated to determine their formation locations in protoplanetary disks. Using the ChemComp code, planet formation modeling was performed, including planetesimal drift, gas and dust accretion, planet migration, stellar elemental abundances, and two additional chemical processes: thermal decomposition of refractory organics and trapping of CO/CO2 in water ice. For nine observed systems, metallicities (C/H and O/H) were calculated and compared with observational constraints. The results show that observed abundances are reproduced when planets form at different positions relative to the H2O and CO2 snow lines. At least six out of nine systems are consistent with formation beyond the water snow line. A joint analysis with orbital parameters (distances, eccentricities, inclinations) indicates that many systems likely underwent dynamical scattering followed by tidal evolution.
threads: Большинство горячих юпитеров, пышущих жаром у самого лица своих звёзд, на самом деле носят ледяное прошлое. Химия их атмосфер — как клеймо на перегретом паровозе, сошедшем с рельсов: она выдает рождение далеко за снеговой чертой, где вода замерзала в лёд. Это значит, что системы пережили гравитационные катастрофы, расшвырявшие планеты к звёздам. Скоро мы сможем читать эти химические летописи для тысяч миров.

title: Neural Cartographer: Recovering Invisible Laws
oneliner: A hybrid method recovers hidden dynamics, like a cartographer creating an accurate map from fragmentary landmarks.
description: Scientists have created a method that completes partial equations in physics and biology. Known laws serve as landmarks, and a neural network, like a cartographer, draws uncharted regions by learning from available measurements. This improves forecast accuracy while keeping the model interpretable.
abstract: A hybrid neuro-physical approach is proposed for ordinary differential equations (ODEs), where known components are kept explicit and unknown ones are approximated by a neural network. The method alternates two stages: recovering hidden states via an RTS smoother (Rauch–Tung–Striebel) with fixed parameters, and training the network via backpropagation on smoothed trajectories. Iterations continue until a criterion is met. Effectiveness is tested on linear, nonlinear, and stiff systems with partial observation. In all cases, missing ODE components are learned from incomplete data, interpretable structure is preserved, and accuracy of hidden state reconstruction and long-term forecasting is improved.

title: Underwater Postman Robot with Charging
oneliner: An underwater robot uses light to locate sensors and smartly manages its energy — either recharging them or just collecting data.
description: The robot spots sensors by their faint glow and then decides: if the battery is almost dead, it recharges; if it's half-full, it first gathers data then tops it up; if full, it simply reads. This strategy extends the underwater network’s lifespan and conserves the robot’s own power. A simple equatio
abstract: For underwater optical communication (UWOC), the energy budget of nodes limits long-term operation. A mobile system is investigated where an AUV simultaneously transmits data and wirelessly charges a network of randomly distributed sensors. A comprehensive mission model is developed, combining stochastic node discovery (based on SNR, with derivation of the detection distance distribution) and state-aware servicing. The SA-OPS strategy is proposed: based on the node's energy level, a choice is made between proactive charging, communication with charging, or communication only. Simulation and multi-criteria analysis demonstrate that SA-OPS improves the balance between AUV energy consumption and network energy health relative to baseline strategies. The charging threshold is approximated by a simple state-based heuristic, providing a practical tool for autonomous energy replenishment underwater.

title: How to fish out a friend's voice from a noisy conversation
oneliner: A new competition teaches algorithms to fish out a friend's voice from real hubbub, not studio silence — with interruptions, echo, and the hiss of a coffee maker.
description: You recorded a group's chatter, but you want to hear just one voice. Until now, such systems were trained on artificial mixes without echo or noise. Now the REAL-TSE Challenge has launched — a competition on real recordings with interruptions and street noise. Participants create an algorithm that,
abstract: The REAL-TSE competition, held as part of IEEE SLT 2026, focused on target speaker extraction from real conversation recordings. Participants were given a multi-channel mixture and one or more samples of the target speaker's voice; they had to recover only that speech. Unlike synthesized tests, this used English and Chinese recordings with natural overlaps, reverberation, noise, channel mismatch, and conversational dynamics. The competition included two tracks: online (streaming extraction with low latency) and offline (processing with full context). Evaluation was based on Token Error Rate, Speaker Similarity, DNSMOS, and F1 score of target speaker activity. The overview paper describes the task formulation, datasets, baseline solutions, evaluation protocol, submitted systems, analysis by conditions, and conclusions for future benchmarks.

title: Sulfur Photochemistry as an Indicator of Mantle Redox States in Rocky Planets
oneliner: Photochemical reactions of sulfur-bearing molecules in exoplanet atmospheres allow remote probing of their interior geochemistry.
description: This study explores the role of photochemistry in shaping the observed spectra of rocky exoplanets and the potential use of sulfur compounds to diagnose mantle redox states. Through coupled planetary evolution and chemical kinetics modeling, it is shown that while the bulk atmosphere is controlled b
abstract: The question of what determines the composition of rocky exoplanet atmospheres—interior degassing or non-equilibrium processes like photochemistry—remains open. Using the PROTEUS computational model, coupled with FastChem and VULCAN chemical codes, evolutionary simulations were conducted for a wide range of mantle redox states, irradiation fluxes, and stellar spectra (solar-type and M-dwarfs). Comparisons were made between thermochemical equilibrium, vertical transport only, and combined transport and photochemistry. They found that even with non-equilibrium chemistry, the bulk atmosphere is controlled by the mantle's redox state and degassing history: reduced interiors lead to H₂-dominated atmospheres, oxidized interiors to CO₂-dominated ones. Photochemistry affects the upper layers, depleting neutral volatile compounds and enhancing radical concentrations, especially under high irradiation. SO₂ abundance increases significantly at intermediate and oxidized mantle states. Synthetic emission spectra reveal SO₂ absorption bands at 4 and 7.3/8.7 μm with amplitudes of ~60 and ~100 ppm, which drop to ~30 and ~50 ppm for oxidized mantles.
threads: Палимпсест атмосферы: звезда переписывает химию, но сера сопротивляется. SO₂ на экзопланетах как древняя строка, проступающая сквозь новый текст. Мантия выдыхает газы, фотохимия скраблит пергамент, а мы видим только глубокий след окисления. Так геология становится видимой в телескоп. Будущая миссия Ariel превратит это в карту недр.

title: How arterial pulse moves fluid in the brain
oneliner: A simplified model shows how pulsing arteries act as pumps, pushing cleansing fluid through spongy tissue.
description: A mathematical model of fluid flow around brain arteries boiled down to a single equation. Flexible walls and a porous structure are key to efficient brain waste clearance.
abstract: Based on the model of peristaltic flow in non-axisymmetric annular channels with rigid walls proposed by Coenen et al. (2021) for periarterial spaces, the problem is generalized to account for porous resistance (Darcy–Brinkman term in the axial momentum equation) and two-way fluid-structure interaction with a compliant outer wall. Changes in hydraulic resistance due to peristalsis and wall displacements are treated perturbatively, reducing the problem to a single nonlinear partial differential equation for axial pressure. This approach enables parametric studies and deepens the understanding of flow in porous, penetrable periarterial spaces. Analytical solutions are obtained for small-amplitude peristaltic waves.

title: The Illusion of Accuracy: How AI Testing in Acoustics Misleads
oneliner: The testing method matters more than the algorithm: data leakage creates an illusion of accurate acoustic prediction.
description: High AI accuracy in acoustics is often an illusion caused by data leakage during testing. Honest validation crushes it severalfold, but even then, algorithms accurately measure loudness and decay time, and most importantly, masterfully reconstruct the sound field between sensors.
abstract: We analyze how the validation protocol affects the accuracy of models predicting room acoustic parameters (ISO 3382-1) from sparse measurements. Using data from a conference hall (264 seats) and a concert hall (180 seats), a factorial experiment was conducted: splitting by rows or grouping by positions, features either with measurements in the test set or only geometry and environment. When splitting by rows with test measurements, the average R² for key parameters was 0.81; with positional grouping without them, R² drops to 0.09–0.57. The hybrid CNN, using the impulse response of the test point, extracts a positional fingerprint from it, not acoustics; when trained only on training signals, the advantage disappears for all parameters. In a realistic protocol, the scatter among models is an order of magnitude smaller than between protocols, but trained models still perform better for sound strength and reverberation time. High accuracy returns when interpolating conditions at measured points (band-averaged R² 0.80–0.88)—a separate useful task.

title: A Smart Navigator That Doesn’t Trust Itself
oneliner: A neural network notices when a standard tracking algorithm starts making mistakes and retrains itself in a fraction of a second without human help.
description: A self‑learning module has been built into drone and satellite tracking software. It senses that the old rules are no longer working and instantly adapts, making predictions more accurate in any unstable environment.
abstract: Reliable state estimation in dynamic systems is challenged by model mismatch, unknown noise statistics, and temporal variations. Classic adaptive filters, including neural network-enhanced extensions like KalmanNet, are sensitive to distribution shifts and lack autonomous adaptation mechanisms. CASA-KalmanNet is proposed, a framework with a CPDNet module that analyzes interpretable internal features of KalmanNet and produces soft indicators of reliability degradation. These indicators dynamically govern online learning, enabling timely and data-efficient adaptation to both abrupt and gradual system changes without requiring new ground-truth labels from the shifted regime. Numerical experiments on linear and nonlinear state-space models show that CASA-KalmanNet consistently outperforms existing trainable filters under model mismatch, closely approaching the accuracy of optimal classical methods.

title: How AI Stopped Mixing Up Sounds in a Script
oneliner: An AI conductor keeps things in line: a new method forces audio generators to follow the script more strictly.
description: When a neural network turns text into sound, it easily messes up the order of events. The solution is a judge model that listens to the recording and checks it against the script. Based on its assessments, it teaches the generator not to confuse a ring with a door slam. The new S3Bench test confirme
abstract: Modern text-to-audio models achieve impressive synthesis quality but often violate instructions involving multiple sound events and their temporal order. The issue stems from existing metrics and training signals that prioritize global quality over precise instruction following. We propose an instruction-level control method that uses audio-aware large language models (ALLMs) to perform fine-grained assessments of target event presence and temporal relationships in generated audio. After validating ALLM judgments against benchmarks and human verification, we convert the feedback into preference pairs for direct preference optimization. We also introduce S3Bench, a new benchmark for evaluating narrative instruction following with multiple events and timestamps. Experiments show that our approach improves event completeness, temporal ordering, and joint instruction-following accuracy on existing benchmarks and S3Bench, while preserving overall sound quality.

title: Radio Waves Paint Portraits of Obstacles
oneliner: Radio signal distortions reveal a precise 'portrait' of an obstacle — its size, shape, and distance.
description: A radio signal bending around a building creates a pattern of peaks and fades — a radio portrait. Scientists have developed a method that reads these invisible 'brushstrokes' and reconstructs the exact appearance, size, and location of the obstacle. It uses only ordinary frequencies, yet accuracy re
abstract: A rigorous physics-consistent parametric model of a diffraction channel for sensor-based object detection at wireless communication frequencies is proposed. Maximum likelihood methods for estimating obstacle shape, range, and angles of arrival are developed, and the Cramér-Rao bound, which sets the fundamental accuracy limit, is derived. The model integrates far-field approximations, paraxial Fresnel, and exact near-field, ensuring broad applicability. It is shown that the estimation problem scales with the Fresnel number, linking carrier frequency, object size, and distance, making the approach frequency-independent. Numerical experiments confirm that maximum likelihood estimates approach the Cramér-Rao bound at moderate to high signal-to-noise ratios, demonstrating high accuracy of diffraction-based obstacle sensing.

title: Imitation Drone Dodges Black Holes of Uncertainty
oneliner: The drone copies an ace's flight, but knows where the 'black holes' are: it automatically steers clear of zones where even a tiny mistake leads to a crash.
description: The algorithm teaches to copy the best maneuvers but adds insurance: if reality differs from training, the drone itself realizes the old path is dangerous and builds a safe detour, avoiding 'black hole' zones. This makes delivery and rescue drones invulnerable to surprises.
abstract: Imitation learning is sensitive to distribution shifts, creating safety risks. A distributed-robust and safe architecture is proposed that explicitly accounts for two types of shifts: policy-induced shifts and uncertainty-induced shifts. The core of the method is a combination of Taylor series-based imitation learning (TaSIL), which mitigates the effects of policy shifts, and uncertainty-robust adaptive control, which handles environmental disturbances. This architecture enables formulation of an optimization problem that ensures safe behavior under uncertainty with hard safety constraints. Effectiveness is demonstrated on a UAV: the drone completes a mission in an unstable environment while avoiding predefined danger zones.

title: Space modules heal wounds without commands
oneliner: Modular satellites can now close punctures on their own, as if sealing a wound.
description: A self-repair algorithm for cube-shaped module satellites. When punctured, surviving blocks, like cells in a wound, crawl toward the hole and restore the shape from memory — without blueprints or commands. The more modules, the more precise the reassembly.
abstract: Damage in modular spacecraft disrupts mechanical and communication links, reducing overall functionality. Traditional approaches use redundancy or pre-planned reconfiguration and do not provide autonomous repair with only local information and physical constraints. A fully decentralized asynchronous strategy mimicking biological wound healing is proposed: the spacecraft is modeled as a lattice-constrained graph; local alarm signals guide surviving modules to breaches to pull together tears, after which each module locally restores its previous shape along its own trajectory, without absolute positioning. Efficiency was evaluated in a realistic PyBullet simulation for structures of up to 160 modules, three failure levels (10, 20, 30%), and random or localized damage. Even with 30% randomly failed modules, the algorithm gathers approximately 80% or more of the remaining ones into a single connected component, and this fraction grows with system size, making the approach highly scalable for large swarm spacecraft.

title: Untangling Layered Radio Modulation: The TSDN Method
oneliner: A neural network archaeologist separates hidden layers of signal encoding.
description: Engineers built the TSDN neural network, which acts like an archaeologist, separating tangled layers of modulation in radio signals. It shifts the signal into logarithmic space, where layers add instead of multiply, and learns to accurately reconstruct even unfamiliar combinations, staying locked on
abstract: Automatic composite modulation recognition (ACMR) is a key task for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Traditional approaches suffer from semantic entanglement of layers and degradation due to hardware distortions.
