A neural network TSDN is proposed, with a disentangled semantic space and zero-shot learning. Logarithmic mapping linearizes the mixing of layers, and a learnable geometric transformation extracts layer-wise features. A multi-task loss function improves generalization. Accuracy for unknown modulations is over 93%, and the method remains operational at SNR down to 4 dB under fading and receiver imperfections. This paves the way for adaptive systems that require no retraining.

title: Frugal Radar: Powering Up Only When the Target Slips Away
oneliner: By predicting motion, the system turns off its transmitter and saves up to 50% energy—like astronomers waiting for an exoplanet transit.
description: Future 6G networks will merge data transmission and radar. Constant scanning is costly, but there's a solution: akin to astronomical transit observations, measurements are taken only when uncertainty arises. An algorithm, honed on the Apollo missions, halves power consumption without sacrificing lin
abstract: Energy efficiency is critical for 6G ISAC systems, as constant sensing requires high power even with stable communication. A beamforming method is proposed for dual-purpose MIMO systems (communication and radar) that minimizes radiated power while guaranteeing a given SINR for users and reliable tracking of multiple targets. The innovation lies in adaptive sensing skips: based on an extended Kalman filter, posterior confidence and normalized innovation squared (NIS) are computed, and the radar is activated only when information is lacking. Robustness during skips is ensured by sector constraints on the beampattern and a safe level of background illumination. Results show significant energy savings without degrading communication and with minimal impact on localization accuracy.

title: The Musical Horizon: How a Song Gains Dimension
oneliner: Artificial intelligence turns music into an emotional 360-degree video.
description: The algorithm breaks down a song into emotions in four-bar steps, then creates a panoramic video that changes with the mood. The user finds themselves inside an animated painting born from sound.
abstract: A pipeline for generating 360-degree videos from music is presented, taking into account the emotional trajectory of the composition. For an input song, valence and arousal values are first predicted every four bars. The resulting estimates are transformed into visual control vectors using EmotiCrafter, then undergo fine semantic tuning via the SEGA framework for keyframe generation. Image-to-video models synthesize continuous panoramic videos from these keyframes. The result is 360-degree visualizations reflecting the emotional development and temporal structure of the song. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated on diverse music genres and qualitatively compared with the baseline approach From-Sound-To-Sight.

title: AI Judges Listen Not with Ears, but with Labels
oneliner: AI speech assessment systems often rely on textual cues rather than the sound itself.
description: Experiments show that speech assessment algorithms ignore the sound and focus on textual labels. Like a critic who reads the menu but doesn’t taste the dish, such judges score based on the description. Even when their scores match human evaluations, they cannot be trusted in high-stakes tests.
abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) are deployed as automatic judges for speech evaluation, but high correlation with human ratings does not mean verdicts are based on audio. An audit of protocol 'shortcuts' was conducted in three typical protocols: feature-blueprint judging (judgment from textual descriptions of acoustic features), reference-based judging, and pairwise A/B comparison. Across six judges and four attributes, many models were found to exploit shortcuts. For instance, when audio is replaced with a structured text description containing deliberately incorrect labels, five models' emotion assessment accuracy drops to 0.10 or below. In concatenated A/B comparisons, Qwen3-Omni-Thinking often selects the same slot regardless of sample order. Results indicate that aggregate agreement metrics can overestimate judgment reliability unless the model and protocol are analyzed jointly; a dedicated shortcut probe is necessary for each model-protocol pair.
